Product tour

The whole thing, on one page.

Six screens, in the order a week actually runs through them: a lead arrives, a unit is held, stock is checked, an order is promised, money is chased, and the tax credit is reconciled. Every label is the one the software uses.

Get a scope and a numberHow a project runs
  1. Ordence
  2. Product
  3. Product tour

It starts with somebody asking

An enquiry lands, gets an owner in seconds, and carries a coloured edge the moment its follow-up is due. Nothing sits unclaimed over a weekend, which is the single most expensive thing that happens in a small sales team.

This one is live. Drag a card between columns, or focus one and use the left and right arrow keys. Nothing is saved — it resets when you reload.

Then it has to be deliverable

Available is on hand minus what is already promised — the only figure safe to quote against. Late orders are counted in rupees rather than in count, because six small ones are not the same meeting as one large one.

Ready to see this against your own numbers?

Get a scope and a number

What the money side looks like

The dashboard you open to, the tax screens nobody enjoys, and the statements that are derived from the ledger rather than rebuilt from it every month.

And then it has to be collected

Ageing computed once and rendered everywhere, so the number on the screen is the number in the export. And input tax credit matched line by line against what your suppliers actually filed, with the money at risk named.

Ready to see this against your own numbers?

Get a scope and a number

These are rebuilt in HTML rather than pasted in as screenshots, so they stay sharp at any size and load in kilobytes. Every column heading, status word and empty-state sentence is copied from the application source — if a label here is wrong, it is wrong because the software changed and this page has not caught up yet.

See it against your own data.

Where it is useful we load a sample of your real records, so you are looking at your own customers rather than a demo tenant full of invented ones.
